summary: João Franco (1855–1929) broke from the Regenerators to found his own party and was called to the presidency of the council in 1906 on a promise to clean up the rotation from inside it. In May 1907 he dissolved parliament and governed by decree with the king’s consent, jailing and deporting opponents; it was that government the regicides of February 1908 set out to end, and it fell within days of the killing. He is in the atlas as the man whose dictatorship put the crown on one side of a political fight it could not afford to lose.
